The skill’s project-relative helper path is not present in this checkout, so I’m rerunning the same helper from its installed location. This is a review-only task, so the skill is guiding the audit criteria rather than causing any code changes.

The first direct pass has isolated the highest-risk area: the new hold gesture is stateful across pointer, keyboard, async permission, transcription, and component remounts. I’m now checking those transitions against the recorder/provider contracts and the generated browser-runtime bundle, not just the JSX.

content.text: The focused selector tests and TypeScript check pass, but they do not exercise the gesture state machine. I’ve also confirmed the generated NodePod snapshot still contains the old gating expression, so the source and browser sandbox are currently inconsistent. I’m doing one final full web-test pass and then I’ll return only non-duplicative findings.

      "issueCode": "resource_leakage",
      "description": "The new keyboard-mode switch can unmount SpeechComposerControl while press-and-hold capture is active, but no unmount cleanup calls MicRecorder.cancel(). This can leave the MediaRecorder and microphone tracks running indefinitely, including when the recorder promise resolves after unmount.",

    },

      "issueCode": "logic_error",
      "description": "A pointer cancellation is handled as a successful release, causing partial audio from an aborted mobile or OS-interrupted gesture to be uploaded and transcribed. onPointerCancel should call the recorder's cancel() method instead.",
